<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-docs.mjs from the repository. Do not edit here. -->
grandstack-web is a single-page React app that talks to grandstack-server over GraphQL. It is a movie and people search, filter, compare and edit app, written to show what a GraphQL-on-Neo4j front end looks like and to be adapted to your own data.

Applies to grandstack-web v0.5.1 (React 19, Vite 8, urql 5, GraphQL Code Generator, TypeScript).

## Stack

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI | React 19 + react-router 8 | Client-side routes; nginx falls back to `index.html`. |
| GraphQL client | urql 5 with `cacheExchange` and `fetchExchange` | Default request policy is `cache-and-network`. |
| Types | GraphQL Code Generator, client preset | Operations written with the `graphql()` tag are typed from the live schema. |
| Animation | `motion` | Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| Graph view | `react-force-graph-2d` (MIT) | Neo4j's own NVL has a custom licence, so it is not used. |
| Styling | Plain CSS with design tokens | `src/theme/tokens.css`, styled after Neo4j's Needle design system (see [customising](/docs/grandstack-web/customising/#about-needle)). |
| Posters, avatars | Generated in the browser | No image files. |

## Folder map

```
src/
  main.tsx                 urql client, router, motion config
  App.tsx                  routes, header, Add menu, compare tray, theme toggle
  pages/                   one component per route (Home, Results, MovieDetail, MovieNew, MovieEdit,
                           People, PersonDetail, PersonNew, PersonEdit, Compare)
  search/                  FilterSidebar, MovieCard, PersonCard
  forms/                   MovieForm, PersonForm, PersonPicker, DeleteButtons, and model.ts (pure logic)
  graph/                   GraphView (shared), MovieGraph, PersonGraph
  lib/                     filters.ts, peopleFilters.ts (URL state and GraphQL where/sort), compare.tsx,
                           hash.ts and initials.ts (small helpers used by posters and avatars)
  poster/Poster.tsx        generated poster art
  ui/                      Button, Chip, Checkbox, RatingBadge, Skeleton, Avatar, ConfirmDialog, PublicEditBanner
  theme/tokens.css         colours, spacing, radii, light and dark
  styles.css               all component styles
  graphql/generated/       committed output of codegen (do not edit)
e2e/                       browser end-to-end checks (see e2e/README.md)
codegen.ts                 where the schema comes from and which files hold operations
nginx.conf, Dockerfile     production image
```

## Routes

| Path | Page | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | Home | Hero search, genre chips, top rated, newest, most prolific actors and directors |
| `/movies` | Results | Faceted search with filters in the URL |
| `/movies/new` | MovieNew | Create a movie |
| `/movies/:title` | MovieDetail | Facts, cast, graph, recommendations |
| `/movies/:title/edit` | MovieEdit | Edit or delete a movie |
| `/people` | People | Browse people by role |
| `/people/new` | PersonNew | Create a person |
| `/people/:name` | PersonDetail | Stats, filmography, collaborators, graph |
| `/people/:name/edit` | PersonEdit | Edit or delete a person |
| `/compare` | Compare | Up to four movies side by side |
| `/new` | redirect | Goes to `/movies/new` |

Titles and names are the keys, so they appear URL-encoded in paths (`/people/Timoth%C3%A9e%20Chalamet`).

## Data flow

State lives in the **URL**, not in component state, for anything a user might want to share or reload:

[![In grandstack-web the URL query string is parsed into a Filters object, turned into typed GraphQL variables, sent with urql, rendered, and any filter change is written back to the URL.](/diagrams/grandstack-web/url-state-data-flow.svg)](diagrams/url-state-data-flow.svg)

*Figure: one loop from the URL to the screen and back. Click the image for full size; the numbered notes below carry the same information as text.*

1. **The URL is the source of truth.** Filters live in the query string (`g`, `d`, `r`, `rt`, `p`, `s`, `q`), so results are shareable, reloadable and work with the back button.
2. **Pure functions in the middle.** `parseFilters`, `buildWhere` and `buildSort` turn the query string into the `where` and `sort` variables; they are unit-tested. `buildWhere` can leave one facet out, which is how facet counts work.
3. **Typed documents.** Every operation is written with `graphql()` and typed by `npm run codegen` against the live schema, so a wrong field fails at codegen or `tsc`.
4. **Components only render and emit events.** A changed filter calls `serializeFilters` and `setSearchParams`, which closes the loop. Text inputs keep local state and debounce the URL update, otherwise fast typing drops characters.
5. **Almost nothing else is stored.** Only the compare list and the theme are kept in `localStorage`.

- `src/lib/filters.ts` owns the movie filters (`q`, `g` genres, `d` decades, `r` minimum rating, `rt` maximum runtime, `p` person, `s` sort). `src/lib/peopleFilters.ts` owns the people filters (`q`, `role`, `mf` minimum films, `s`). Both are pure functions with unit tests.
- Text inputs that write to the URL keep **local state and debounce** the URL update (see `People.tsx`). Binding an input straight to the URL drops characters when typing fast, because the URL update is asynchronous.
- The compare selection (`localStorage` key `grandstack.compare`, at most four titles) and the theme (`grandstack.theme`) are the only browser-stored state.
- Every GraphQL document is written next to the component that uses it with the `graphql()` tag from `src/graphql/generated`. Codegen validates it against the live schema and generates the result types, so a typo in a field name fails at codegen time and a wrong use of a result field fails at `tsc`.

## Caching and freshness

The urql client uses `requestPolicy: "cache-and-network"`: pages show cached data immediately and always refetch, so lists and counts are fresh after an edit without wiring cache invalidation by hand. Edit forms use `network-only` so they never start from stale data. The server refreshes stored film counts after every mutation, so a refetch after a save is correct.

## Build and deploy

`npm run build` type-checks and builds static files with Vite. The `Dockerfile` builds them and serves them with unprivileged nginx on port 8080, with long-lived caching for `/assets/` and a fallback to `index.html` for client routes.

`VITE_GRAPHQL_URL` is **baked in at build time** (a build argument in the Dockerfile, default `http://localhost:4000/graphql`). It must be a URL the *browser* can reach, not a container-internal hostname. The server's `CORS_ORIGIN` must allow the web origin.
